text: The four war-AI fixes in builds/war-log (exact assault forecast, true-odds attack floor, sacrifice by expected value, visible armies raise the alert; GitLab !48 and !49, on by default) make the AI harder for the human to conquer. Assumption, not checked: games 1-3 were played with DLLs before these fixes.

text: The human takes AI cities on the turn it declares, after staging its units next to them at peace (study/staging.md: games 1-5). The AI cannot answer by construction: a city's danger counts only units of a team already at war and only on the city's own area, so a staged army or one aboard ships counts nothing, and the defenders a city wants do not rise. A city that sizes its defence by the exact assault forecast of the foreign units able to reach it this turn, at peace or at war and aboard ships, loses fewer cities to that strike.

change: Change S on (define AI_STAGED_FORECAST, per mille, off at 0): in CvCityAI::AI_neededDefenders, the land units able to attack that could reach the city this turn, of teams that are not the owner's, its vassal or its master, counted by their moves (units aboard a ship by the ship's moves), are given to AI_assaultForecast against the city's defenders; while the forecast is at least the threshold (AI_STAGED_FORECAST plus ten times the leader's attack-odds change), the city wants one defender more than it has, and while it would be at least the threshold with one defender fewer, it keeps the ones it has. An AI at peace counts another AI's units only if its attitude allows war (the test of the paranoia code); a human's always. Built on the war-log DLL with the four war-AI fixes (builds/staging); only games written by builds made under P3 count, so games for P2 and for P3 never mix.

reason: Before any evidence or build: measured on the saves of games 3 to 5 (HARNESS_DEFENCE_DIAG), raising the defenders a city wants changes them in 6 of 511 AI cities, since city production reads that count only once the city is in danger and about half of all AI cities are already below it. The change is replaced by P4, which also feeds the city's danger flag.

change: Change S2 on (define AI_STAGED_FORECAST, per mille, off at 0). The staged forecast: the land units able to attack that could reach the city this turn, of teams that are not the owner's, its vassal or its master, counted by their moves (units aboard a ship by the ship's moves), given to AI_assaultForecast against the city's land defenders; an AI at peace counts another AI's units only if its attitude allows war (the test of the paranoia code), a human's always. The threshold is AI_STAGED_FORECAST plus ten times the leader's attack-odds change. While the forecast reaches the threshold, the city is in danger (CvCityAI::AI_isDanger, which city production and the city governor read) and wants one defender more than it has (AI_neededDefenders); while it would reach it with one defender fewer, it keeps the ones it has. Danger as unit moves and workers read it (CvPlayerAI::AI_getPlotDanger) is unchanged. Built on the war-log DLL with the four war-AI fixes (builds/staging); only games written by builds made under P4 count, so games for P2 and for P4 never mix.

text: No AI ever moves against the human, even while it leads and while it is at war with one of them (study/doctrine.md, R2: games 1-5). By construction: every war path of CvTeamAI::AI_doWar wants a target weaker than the AI alone and passes a no-war roll against the leader's NoWarAttitudeProbs for its attitude, which the human keeps high with gifts and open borders (R3); the one coalition path (dogpile) counts only the power of teams already at war with the target; and a team with any war plan does not consider a new war. Measured first at the saves (study/d3-design.md, step 1). AIs that weigh a hegemon by their leader's own envy and count the others who would join take more back from the human and let it take less.

change: Change B (study/d3-design.md): step 1, HARNESS_WAR_DIAG, the per-team gates of AI_doWar towards every met team at a save (reads only); step 2, the balance term against a hegemon (define AI_BALANCE_SHARE, per mille of the summed power of the met living teams, off at 0), with the no-war roll against a hegemon lowered by the leader's iWorseRankDifferenceAttitudeChange and kept at ATTITUDE_FRIENDLY, and of candidates (b) the dogpile power counting the teams whose own roll passes and (c) a team with war plans only against teams weaker than the hegemon considering the hegemon by the dogpile path, the ones step 1 shows blocking. Built on the S2 DLL (builds/balance); only games written by builds made under P5 count.

Harness runs of change B: the turn-0 scenario of game 3 (Marathon, Noble), 300 turns, seat 12 played by the human model (HarnessHuman.cpp, policy both.txt of the human-model experiment), the other seats by the AI. One harness DLL, built from the source of P5 (the S2 commit plus change B), in both arms; AI_STAGED_FORECAST 250 in both. Arm a: AI_BALANCE_SHARE 110; arm b: AI_BALANCE_SHARE 0, which leaves AI_doWar as in the S2 build. The cities the human-model seat takes are fewer in arm a.

text: The executable sets up a model for every unit and city and graphics for every plot, on screen or not (research/graphics/README.md, R-C), and a large game (300 cities, 2,359 units, 6,386 unit models at 460 AD) ended with its memory allocation failure; a view window holds a fraction of them (R-D). Keeping graphics only around the camera lowers the executable's memory without changing the game or what is on screen. The memory itself is measured only in the real game, by the user (process memory at the 460 AD save with paging on and off, and play past 490 AD); the harness checks that the change neither crashes nor slows the game.

change: Graphics paging (define GRAPHICS_PAGING, 0 = off): the DLL keeps unit and city entities and the feature, route and improvement graphics of plots only within a window around the camera's look-at plot (getLookAtPlot), sized for the farthest zoom the camera defines allow, with a margin; elsewhere it removes the entity and leaves a bare one (as reloadEntity does before setup) and destroys the plot symbols, and sets them up again when the window returns. Entity calls on a paged-out unit or city are skipped and its battles are not animated. The active player's units and cities are never paged out. Arm a: paging on; arm b: the same build with GRAPHICS_PAGING 0; both in the harness with graphics initialised and a camera sweeping the map, from the 460 AD autosave of the user's Mediterranean game, seeds from ledger.py seeds.

text: What the DLL asks the executable to build scales with the map and with every team's sight: 7,868 yield symbols and a flag per plot with a seen unit exist whether or not on screen, and 552 of 2,132 billboard rebuilds in three harness turns follow other teams' visibility changes, which the billboard does not show (research/graphics/README.md, R-G, R-I). Paging symbols and flags with the units, dirtying billboards only for the active team, and dropping the billboard debug logging lower the executable's memory and work without changing the game or the screen. The executable's memory and time are measured only in the real game, by the user; the harness checks that the changes neither crash nor slow the game.

text: The game froze when the user founded the first city with the paging build (PythonDbg.log ends after 'City Built Event: London' and the score update; LSystem.log has just laid out the city). Of what paging destroys, only the plot builder is never destroyed by vanilla during a game (CvPlot::uninit alone calls PlotBuilderIFace destroy; feature, route, yield and flag symbols and unit and city entities are destroyed and remade in vanilla play), and plot builders share the executable's L-system with city layouts, the first of which is made at the first city. Keeping plot builders removes the freeze. Contradicted if the game still freezes at the first city with GRAPHICS_PAGING_PLOT_BUILDERS 0, or does not freeze with it 1. The harness has no executable, so only the user's game decides; separately CvGameInterface.getCameraZoom took no argument and failed once (PythonErr.log).

change: On top of the graphics rendering bundle (GitLab claude/graphics-paging, tree 04ac18c6): paging is split into switches GRAPHICS_PAGING_UNITS, GRAPHICS_PAGING_CITIES, GRAPHICS_PAGING_PLOTS (feature and route symbols) and GRAPHICS_PAGING_PLOT_BUILDERS, the last 0, so plot builders are no longer destroyed; GRAPHICS_PAGING_SYMBOLS stays; a plot remembers what its page-out removed and its guards and page-in cover only that; CvGameInterface.getCameraZoom takes the argument list. Harness: scenario runs set up graphics with HARNESS_GRAPHICS, and HARNESS_ACTIVE=<player> sets an active player, which the real game always has (without one CvPlot::calculateYield's display branch reads before an array and the harness crashes in either arm). Arm a: this build, defines as shipped; arm b: the same build with GRAPHICS_PAGING 0. Both from turn 0 of the user's Huge Mediterranean WorldBuilder map (all seats AI, HARNESS_ACTIVE=0, camera sweeping one plot per update), 5 turns per run, so every capital is founded, seeds from ledger.py seeds. This checks only that the DLL change neither crashes nor hangs; the freeze is in the executable and is judged by the user's game.

text: Graphics paging pages plots and the units on them separately, so a plot under a unit or city that keeps its graphics (the active player's always do) loses its flag, yield symbols and route symbol, and route symbols go missing next to plots that keep theirs. The unchanged game never shows a unit without its flag or a revealed route without its symbol; the executable calls CvPlot::updateFlagSymbol, getFlagSymbol, getRouteSymbol and isRoute itself. The user's game crashed at the first unit moved with GitLab main d929b57. A harness that does what the executable does near the camera (updateFlagSymbols, then the checks) finds such states with d929b57 (100 turns from turn 0 of the Huge Mediterranean map: 27 flagless live units and 58 routes without symbol with the camera on the active player's units) and none with the DLL before paging. Keeping a plot's graphics while anything on it keeps its own, bringing the plot back with any unit or city that gets its graphics, rebuilding it when the executable asks for a flag there, and never paging routes, leaves none. Contradicted if the game still crashes or freezes with the change, or if the checks find such a state with it.

change: On GitLab main d929b57: CvPlot::canPageGraphicsOut keeps a plot's graphics while a unit or city on it keeps its own or the move being shown goes there; CvGame::pageGraphics pages a plot out after its units and city; CvUnit::setupGraphical, CvUnit::pageGraphics(true), CvUnit::setXY (the plot moved to) and CvCity::setupGraphical, CvCity::pageGraphics(true) bring the plot back first; CvPlot::updateFlagSymbol brings a paged-out plot back when a unit there keeps its graphics or the move goes there; route symbols are never paged (GRAPHICS_PAGING_PLOTS pages feature symbols only); GRAPHICS_PAGING_ZOOM defaults to 0. Harness: plot symbols, features, routes, flags and plot builders are tokens; HARNESS_CAMERA_FOLLOW=1 moves the camera from one unit of the active player to the next; HH_graphicsCheck does what the executable does near the camera and counts states the unchanged game never shows. Arm a: this build; arm b: GitLab main d929b57. Both from turn 0 of the user's Huge Mediterranean WorldBuilder map (all seats AI, HARNESS_ACTIVE=0, camera sweeping the map one plot every 5 calls, a check every update), 20 turns per run, seeds from ledger.py seeds. The crash itself is in the executable and is judged by the user's game.

text: What the screen shows follows from the camera: its eye and target (CyCamera GetCurrentPosition, GetLookAt), the frustum of FIELD_OF_VIEW (42 degrees, GlobalDefines.xml, which the executable reads through CvGlobals::getFIELD_OF_VIEW) and the screen's aspect ratio, cast onto the map's ground plane in world units of PLOT_SIZE (180) per plot (CvMap::plotXToPointX). A paging window taken from that footprint plus a margin holds everything the screen shows at any zoom, pitch and turn of the camera, where the fixed window (40 east and west, 40 north, 16 south) does not: at 6000 units and 28 degrees of pitch the screen reaches 100 plots north. Contradicted if the game shows units, cities or features without graphics with the camera window, or if the window the DLL computes differs from the geometry.

change: On GitLab claude/paging-coherence 006b7840 (P12): with GRAPHICS_PAGING_CAMERA 1, CvGame::graphicsWindowFromCamera reads the camera through CvGameInterface.getCameraView (CyCamera GetCurrentPosition and GetLookAt, the screen's resolution, CyEngine isGlobeviewUp), casts the rays through the corners and edge midpoints of the view (FIELD_OF_VIEW vertically, times the aspect ratio horizontally) onto the ground plane, and takes the footprint's extent west, east, north and south of the look-at plot, plus one plot; GRAPHICS_PAGING_RANGE_* remain the window when the camera cannot be read; a side that grows applies at once, a smaller window after GRAPHICS_PAGING_SHRINK_MS (5000); in globe view nothing changes; the zoom scaling (GRAPHICS_PAGING_ZOOM, getCameraZoom) is removed. Harness: HARNESS_CAMERA_VIEW=<distance>,<pitch>,<yaw>,<width>,<height> answers getCameraView with that camera at the look-at plot (HH_cameraView), and the engine gives the landscape's size (HH_landscapeSize). Arm a: this build, HARNESS_CAMERA_VIEW=2200,45,0,1920,1080; arm b: the P12 build (006b7840). Both from turn 0 of the user's Huge Mediterranean WorldBuilder map (all seats AI, HARNESS_ACTIVE=0, camera following the active player's units, a check every update), 20 turns per run, seeds from ledger.py seeds. The screen itself is judged by the user's game.

text: The mod's Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvGameInterface.py, added for the camera in !57 (ccbc1b5, 'the Beyond the Sword file unchanged'), is not the Beyond the Sword file. It defines 49 functions plus the camera's, its gameUtils() returns a plain CvGameUtils.CvGameUtils(), and it never imports CvGameInterfaceFile. Facts: the original BTS SDK in the GitLab repository (beyond-the-sword-sdk-develop-functional.tar.gz) calls 22 CvGameInterface functions that the file lacks (PYGameModule is "CvGameInterface"; among them getUnitCostMod, getBuildingCostMod, getUpgradePriceOverride, getExperienceNeeded, doPillageGold, doCityCaptureGold, getExtraCost, canBuild, cannotFoundCity); the mod ships BUG's CvGameInterfaceFile.py, 'Overrides the use of CvGameUtils with BUG's modular game utils dispatcher', and registers RoMGameUtils through it (Assets/Config/RoMSettings.xml) with RoM's rules for cannotConstruct, cannotDoCivic, getUnitCostMod, getBuildingCostMod, getUpgradePriceOverride, doPillageGold and doCityCaptureGold; PythonCallbackDefines.xml switches the unit cost, building cost, upgrade price, cannot-construct and cannot-do-civic callbacks on, and calculateExperience calls getExperienceNeeded with no switch. Since the mod's file replaces the game's in play, RoM's Python rules have not run since !57. Moving getCameraView to the mod's own CvScreensInterface.py (PYScreensModule, which the DLL already calls) and deleting the mod's CvGameInterface.py restores the game's file and BUG's dispatcher and keeps the camera window. Contradicted if the installed Beyond the Sword Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvGameInterface.py is the same file (49 functions, no CvGameInterfaceFile import), or if a game on main 4ec8ebc applies RoM's missionary cost (75 % under a state religion civic, RoMGameUtils.getUnitCostMod).

change: On GitLab main 4ec8ebc (P13's tree, build 526bbebe2dc9): CvGame::graphicsWindowFromCamera calls getCameraView in PYScreensModule (CvScreensInterface) instead of PYGameModule; getCameraView, unchanged, moves to the mod's Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvScreensInterface.py; the mod's Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvGameInterface.py is deleted, so the game's own file and BUG's dispatcher answer every CvGameInterface call again; Docs/GRAPHICS_PAGING.md says so. Nothing else changes. With the DLL of 4ec8ebc and the new Python, the camera cannot be read and the GRAPHICS_PAGING_RANGE_* window is used. Harness (Python inert; the harness answers getCameraView by name whatever the module): arm a is this build, arm b the build of 4ec8ebc (526bbebe2dc9), both with HARNESS_CAMERA_VIEW=2200,45,0,1920,1080, from turn 0 of PrivateMaps/Mediterranean, Huge.CivBeyondSwordWBSave (all seats AI, HARNESS_ACTIVE=0, HARNESS_GRAPHICS=1, camera following the active player's units, a check every update), 20 turns per run, seeds from ledger.py seeds.
